text: The town library opened a new reading room last spring. The room faces the river, so it is bright most of the day. Volunteers moved about four thousand books into it over two weekends. Since then, the number of weekday visitors has nearly doubled. The staff now plans evening hours for students.

Maria started baking bread when her office closed during the winter. Her first loaves were dense and flat. She learned that her kitchen was too cold for the dough to rise. After she moved the bowl next to the radiator, the bread improved quickly. By March she was selling loaves to her neighbours.

Honeybees communicate the location of food with a waggle dance. The angle of the dance tells other bees the direction relative to the sun. The length of the waggle run encodes the distance. Bees that follow the dance can find flowers several kilometres away. Researchers decoded this system in the 1940s.

The city council voted to close the main street to cars on Sundays. Shop owners were worried at first that they would lose customers. In the first month, however, foot traffic rose and most shops reported higher sales. The council has since extended the trial to Saturdays. A final decision is expected in the autumn.

Our hiking group set out before sunrise to avoid the afternoon heat. The trail climbed steadily through pine forest for three hours. Near the ridge, the trees thinned and the wind picked up. We reached the summit just before noon and ate lunch behind a rock. The descent took half as long as the climb.

Copper has been used for electrical wiring for more than a century. It conducts electricity well and is easy to draw into thin wires. Aluminium is cheaper and lighter, but it expands more when heated. For that reason, aluminium connections need special fittings. Most household wiring therefore still uses copper.

The old ferry stopped running when the new bridge was finished. For years the boat sat rusting at the dock. Last year a local group bought it for one dollar. They repaired the engine and repainted the hull. It now carries tourists on short trips around the harbour.

Sleep researchers asked volunteers to learn a list of word pairs in the evening. Half of the group slept normally, while the other half stayed awake. The next morning, those who had slept recalled more pairs. The effect was strongest for pairs learned just before bed. The study suggests that sleep helps stabilise new memories.

The school replaced its paper timetable with a mobile app this year. Students can now see room changes as soon as they are made. Teachers say that fewer pupils arrive late to class. Some parents complained that the app drains phone batteries. The developers released an update that fixed the problem in October.

Tomatoes were first grown in western South America. Spanish traders brought them to Europe in the sixteenth century. For a long time many Europeans believed the fruit was poisonous. Italian cooks were among the first to use it widely. Today it is a basic ingredient in kitchens around the world.

The factory switched to solar power for its daytime operations. Panels were installed on the roof and over the car park. On sunny days they supply almost all of the electricity the machines need. At night, the factory still draws power from the grid. The owners expect the panels to pay for themselves within seven years.

A heavy storm knocked down several trees along the coast road. Crews worked through the night to clear the fallen branches. By morning, one lane had reopened to traffic. The second lane stayed closed while engineers checked a damaged wall. Officials asked drivers to use the inland route until the repairs were complete.
